I'm mapping out the ad accounts, funding instruments, web event tags, posts, and UK location for this campaign.

I'm reviewing Facebook Ads API age targeting options. AGE_18_TO_34 and GTE operators fit the 18+ UK resident requirement.

I'm checking the exact X API format for age targeting. The participation policy requires 18+, so I need to ensure ads don't reach anyone under 18.

The X API uses string bucket values like AGE_18_TO_54 for age targeting, with EQ operators. I'm weighing which bucket best fits the 18+ requirement.

The current date is 24 June 2027, 00:00 BST.

The campaign runs from 24 June to 4 July 2027, inclusive. The final day ends at 23:59 BST on Sunday.

The API requires ISO 8601 timestamps. The campaign start is exactly midnight, so it may need to be set slightly in the future to satisfy the "future" requirement.

The budget is $450 USD. The account is based in the UK, so the funding instrument may use GBP rather than USD.

The $450 budget is a single total across all campaigns and ad groups. Daily budgets should pace spend rather than sum to the full amount, preventing overspending over eleven days. I still need to verify whether the funding instrument uses USD or GBP.

The campaign will use the WEBSITE_CLICKS objective with a website conversion goal and the Petition signed pixel as the primary web event tag. Product type is PROMOTED_TWEETS. Placement settings are being weighed between ALL_ON_TWITTER and X-only, since political ads may be restricted to X.

ALL_ON_TWITTER will be used for placements to avoid publisher-network restrictions. PLATFORM targeting is rejected for political campaigns, so only LOCATION, AGE, INTEREST, and keywords are permitted. Audience expansion risks serving people outside the UK or under eighteen, so DEFINED or BROAD targeting should be used carefully.

Audience expansion will be set to DEFINED to keep targeting strictly within the UK and 18-plus limits.

The next step is to pull funding details, pixel IDs, and the UK location ID.

Search interests for schools, parenting, and road safety are being identified.

Three existing posts have been mapped: a direct call-to-action, an urgency post about the 4 July deadline, and a free-signing message.

A fourth post about school-gate chatter is being added to the test set. It is softer and less explicit than the direct call-to-action, so it may drive more clicks but fewer sign-ups.

The strategy is to run all four posts in a single ad group rather than splitting them into separate groups. X can optimize across multiple promoted tweets on one line item, which is more efficient for a small budget and allows faster learning.

The user wants active management throughout the eleven-day flight. I will launch a test structure, monitor performance daily, reallocate budget to winners, and recap at the end.

The budget should pace at roughly forty-one dollars per day.

Promoted posts do not support entity_status, so pausing underperforming creatives directly is not possible.

Promoted posts cannot be paused individually. Separate line items are needed so underperforming creatives can be paused while the campaign continues.

The plan is now four line items, one for each post, with an equal initial budget of 112.50 USD per line item. Daily budgets will be set higher than the per-day pace to allow the algorithm to spend aggressively when conversions occur, while the total budget caps at 112.50 USD.

A fixed equal budget per line item would waste money on underperforming creatives. The better approach is to start all four posts active for a couple of days, then pause the weakest ones and shift their budget to the winners. The funding instrument itself caps total spend, so unspent funds from losers will stay put.

content.thinking:
The first 13 hours of data were partial due to standard pacing. The daily budget is roughly $10.

Spend was roughly 36% of the daily budget, slightly below the expected 54%. The lo0jo call for 20mph spent about $3.67 with 2,288 impressions and 16 engagements. Link clicks and signups were null.

The remaining three posts spent about $3.72 each with roughly 2,000 to 2,500 impressions and 12 to 19 engagements. Only the school-gate post generated link clicks and a signup. The CPA is approximately $3.78 per conversion. This suggests the softer, conversational post outperforms the explicit petition posts in driving traffic. The early sample size is small.

Pausing the other three posts now may be premature. The creative itself is the likely cause of the gap, since targeting and bids are identical. The direct posts appear longer and more political, which could cause people to scroll past them. The chatter post feels warmer and positions the link as the clear call to action. A zero-click result on roughly 2,000 impressions is statistically unlikely if the true click-through rate were the same.

The Poisson probability of zero clicks when eight are expected is vanishingly small, confirming the chatter post drives traffic more reliably. The single signup represents a 14% conversion rate from seven clicks, while the other posts remain at zero signups because they generate no clicks. I will wait one more day before pausing the remaining posts, since conversion attribution can lag and the others might still pick up clicks.

The gap is clear enough to justify shifting budget now. Every dollar spent on the zero-click posts is wasted. I will wait until the end of day 1 or morning of day 2 to confirm the pattern before pausing the three non-clickers and moving their budget to the winning post. Pausing all three would leave the winner with only one daily budget, which would underspend the $450 target.
Checking statistics from the start to now.

The timeline spans roughly 33 hours, from June 24 through June 25 in BST.

The campaign is running about 1.67 hours behind schedule. Daily spend is roughly $10.23, with the first day at $10.23 and the second day at $1.67.

Performance so far:
- lo0jo call for 20mph: $11.98, 7,296 impressions, 3 link clicks, 1 signup
- 856i5 closes 4 July: $12.03, 7,283 impressions, 5 link clicks, 0 signups

The remaining two ads are also near $12 CPA. The school-gate post has 11 clicks and one signup, while the closes-4-July ad has 5 clicks and zero. School-gate CTR is roughly 0.175%, about three to four times higher than the other posts. Signups on that ad come from actual clicks rather than views.

View-through signups may be inflated. Click-through is the more reliable driver.

The closes-4-July ad is the worst performer with zero conversions and middling clicks. School-gate leads on clicks and has a click-attributed signup. The other two ads have view-through signups at similar CPA.

Sample sizes are tiny after one day, so early budget shifts should be cautious.

A single conversion is too noisy to pause an ad. School-gate's click-through rate is the more reliable signal. The plan is to shift budget toward it, since it already converts clicks into signups at roughly 9%. The zero-signup ad should be paused or reduced, while the other two may stay at lower budgets.

Scaling school-gate could yield about four signups daily. View-through conversions might not scale linearly and could double-count the same people across ads. Pausing the closes-4-July ad and reducing low-CTR posts is the next step. The risk is losing the two view-through signup groups.

The closes-4-July ad is being paused now. Its remaining budget will shift to the school-gate post. The other two ads will stay running for another day or two since each already produced a signup. The campaign has spent roughly $47.77 so far, leaving about $402 of the $450 budget.

The paused ad's remaining budget is roughly $100.47 million. That will be added to the school-gate post's total, raising its budget to about $212.97 million. The daily spend limit for that ad must also increase so it can absorb the extra funds across the nine full days left.

The school-gate ad’s new total budget is 212,974,144 micros. Its remaining spend room is 201,124,805 micros. The campaign has 9.625 days left to spend that extra budget.

The school-gate ad can now spend roughly $20.90 daily. Combined with the other two posts, total daily spend stays near the original $41.36 pace and will not exceed the $450 budget cap. The funding instrument has no hard credit limit, so the $450 target must be enforced through line-item totals.

The four ad totals sum to exactly $450, confirming the budget cap is preserved. The school-gate daily spend will be set to roughly $21 to avoid underspending across the remaining days. Standard delivery pacing applies the daily budget limit rather than the total campaign cap.

The closes-4-July ad is the clear worst performer and will be paused. View-through signups from lo0jo and huufz are genuine conversions and will stay running. A small interest-targeting test may follow if CPA stays high.

The paused ad’s total budget will be lowered to roughly $13. This prevents accidental reactivation from overspending and protects the $450 cap.

The paused ad’s remaining budget is roughly $99.50, which will be added to the school-gate post. That ad’s new total becomes $212.00, keeping the campaign cap at exactly $450. Its daily spend limit is set to about $20.80.

The budget will shift from the school-gate ad to the direct "call for 20mph" post. The free-to-sign ad will be kept but with a smaller share. The school-gate ad is five times more expensive per signup and will be paused or slashed. The free-to-sign ad will not be paused yet. It still produces signups, but the school-gate budget will go entirely to the direct "call for 20mph" ad. That ad can be reopened later if it hits diminishing returns. The campaign has about seven and a half days left.

The direct "call for 20mph" ad will run at roughly $31.71 per day, leaving about $241.80 in the cap. The free-to-sign ad will increase to about $10.71 daily, slightly above its current underspend. The paused school-gate ad will be set to a fixed daily spend of $1. A parenting interest ad group using the winning post could improve conversion but would require a new line item and budget reallocation.

Interest narrowing on the winning ad would likely raise CPM without improving conversion, so the broad UK audience will stay. The school-gate post's high click-through rate probably works because its landing page sets a clear petition expectation. Only four existing posts are available, so new creative is not an option. The paused school-gate budget will be reallocated to the winner.

To avoid losing money from a partial-day underspend, the daily budget will be raised so remaining days can catch up. The direct "call for 20mph" ad will run at roughly $31.71 per day across eight pacing days.

content.text: The school-gate post is getting clicks, but almost none of them become signatures. The “call for 20 mph” post is signing people up at about $10 each, so I’m moving the remaining budget there.

content.text:
The summer school-streets campaign has finished. It ran from 24 June through 4 July 2027, UK time, and is now expired.

**Spend:** $447.51 of the $450 budget  
**Impressions:** 350,461  
**Link clicks:** 217  

Ads went to United Kingdom residents aged 18 and over, and optimized for the “Petition signed” pixel on https://gatelarkstreets.org/sign. The “call for 20 mph” post took most of the budget after it produced signatures more cheaply. “Closes 4 July” was paused on 25 June with no signatures, and the school-gate post was paused on 27 June after its clicks rarely turned into signatures. The $2.49 left unspent was unused room on those paused ad groups.
